taskTitle: Repo2 backup topology decision and runbook convergence
question: Which off-host repo2 topology is safely supportable on production's current pgBackRest 2.50, given that `backup --repo=2` is refused on the PostgreSQL host with ERROR [072]?

decision.statement: An off-host repo2 with NO repository host, written by the production primary.

rejected.A: Repository-host-driven backup. Requires repo-host -> production SSH, which runbook §16.5 forbids and §22.9's UNREACHABLE_GOOD gate tests for the absence of. Because archive_command runs on the primary by definition, A does not REVERSE the trust direction, it makes it MUTUAL — its exposure is a strict superset of every alternative. It also moves the backup off noramedi-pgbackrest-backup.sh, so the fail-closed repo2 encryption gate stops being enforced by code. R1's own harness retried the backup from the repository host on 2.50 and that retry ALSO failed (ERROR_072_THEN_REPO_HOST_BACKUP_ALSO_FAILED).
rejected.B: Upgrade pgBackRest before activating repo2. Sound but unnecessary. The check was removed in 2.55.0 (2025-04-21, PR 2512), so B's premise is real and its minimum version is exact. But B buys primary-driven backup against a REPOSITORY HOST, and R2 shows the primary already drives repo2 on 2.50 whenever repo2 has no repository host. B would pay a package upgrade on a live PHI database host — plus 2.59.0's new restriction that only `restore` may run as root by default, which would break the existing root-invoked cron wrapper — to obtain a capability already in hand.

decision.decisionScope: Topology only: where `backup` runs, and which way trust flows. The TRANSPORT is a procurement variable and both proven shapes satisfy the topology.

rootCause.finding: ERROR [072] is gated solely on repoN-host being SET. It is not about --repo=2, and not about running backup on the primary.
rootCause.raisedBy: repoIsLocalVerify(), src/protocol/helper.c, called as the first statement of cmdBackup()
rootCause.consequence: A repository with no repository host — object store or SFTP endpoint — is 'local' by this definition, so the check cannot fire and the backup runs on the primary.
rootCause.removedBy: PR 2512, 'Allow backup command to operate on remote repositories', released 2025-04-21
rootCause.bisection: repoIsLocalVerify present through 2.54.2, absent from 2.55.0 onward

experiment.pinVerifiedAgainst: the running binary, not the package name apt reported
experiment.invocationHost: the PostgreSQL host, for every command in every shape

shapes.why: Without this control the harness could only ever confirm. A harness that cannot fail proves nothing — the lesson of R1-F1, where a guard reported CLEAN on precisely the input containing the defect. repo2-host points at a nonexistent host on purpose: the check is a config-time test evaluated before any connection is attempted, so an unreachable host still yields 072 rather than a network error.

experiment.supersedes: R1's 'repo2 RESTORABILITY on 2.50' open item, but ONLY for repo2 shapes with no repository host. The repo2-host shape remains unrestorable on 2.50.

confidentiality.method: 3000 rows carrying a synthetic PHI marker were written and checkpointed, then backed up; the repository's stored bytes were searched for the marker both raw and after attempting to decompress every object.
confidentiality.pgdataInterpretation: PHI is NOT encrypted at rest on the primary. That is the control proving the search works.
confidentiality.repo2Interpretation: The storage operator holds ciphertext only.
confidentiality.envelope: Repository objects carry the OpenSSL `Salted__` AES-256-CBC envelope.
confidentiality.keyBinding: With the passphrase supplied via PGBACKREST_REPO2_CIPHER_PASS but WRONG, `info --repo=2` fails with [FormatError] unable to load info file. With the correct passphrase from the config it reports status: ok, cipher: aes-256-cbc.
confidentiality.notEncrypted: Object and file NAMES. Without repo2-bundle=y the repository leaks PostgreSQL relation paths and per-relation sizes (base/<db-oid>/<relfilenode>), plus stanza name, backup labels and schedule, and WAL volume. Contents are encrypted either way; this is a metadata exposure and is why repo2-bundle=y is published in the config shapes.
confidentiality.rotation: The repo2 passphrase is fixed at stanza-create and CANNOT be rotated in place. It must be escrowed before stanza-create, not after.

transports.note: Both satisfy the selected topology. Selection is a procurement question, and procurement is an external blocker either way.

sftp.rationale: A plain Türkiye VPS. §16 records Türkiye IaaS as market-available, so E1-E5 can be attempted today.
sftp.secondaryRuns: sshd only — no pgBackRest, therefore no version parity to maintain and no remote protocol exposed
sftp.knownCost: The Debian libssh2 build may offer only the SHA-1 `ssh-rsa` signature algorithm, so the endpoint's sshd may need `PubkeyAcceptedAlgorithms +ssh-rsa`, and the keypair must be PEM. Without it the run fails with ERROR [101] libssh2 error [-18] — an AUTH failure, not a topology refusal.
sftp.costScope: Applies to the SECONDARY's authentication posture, never to production. Build-dependent: production's own libssh2 may already negotiate rsa-sha2, so this must be VERIFIED at CHECKPOINT 5 rather than assumed in either direction.

s3.rationale: Better on immutability, and needs no ssh-rsa at all. Blocked only on evidence: no Türkiye-resident S3-compatible provider is evidenced as procurable anywhere in this repository.
s3.uriStyle: pgBackRest defaults to `host`; most non-AWS S3-compatible endpoints need `path`. Getting it wrong presents as a DNS or certificate failure rather than a config error.
mandatoryLifecycleRules: abort incomplete multipart uploads — pgBackRest never issues AbortMultipartUpload, and orphaned parts are billed but invisible to ListObjects
expire noncurrent versions on a versioned bucket — pgBackRest is entirely version-unaware, so its deletes only create delete-markers and storage grows without bound while `expire` reports success
s3.wormWarning: Do NOT enforce immutability by revoking the credential's delete right. `backup` runs `expire` automatically and `expire-auto` is GLOBAL rather than per-repository, so a WORM or object-locked repo2 fails the backup command itself, at the expire stage, AFTER the data has been written. Use a provider-side retention policy instead.

walBacklogMonitoring.whyDefaultsUnchanged: These are ACTIVATION values, not defaults. Flipping a code default would alert on every existing single-repo production host and would break the R1 backward-compatibility contract asserted in noramedi-opscheck.test.sh and pitrStatusContract.test.ts.
walBacklogMonitoring.rejectedApproach: The earlier '25% of free disk' wording was a convention rather than a measurement and was rejected as too permissive. opscheck deliberately takes an absolute byte figure because it never sees the PGDATA filesystem; no auto-derivation may be introduced.
walBacklogMonitoring.activationRequirement: Before repo2 activation the operator must prove readyCount = 0 and walBytes well under 4 GiB. With REQUIRE_WAL_BACKLOG=true and either limit still 0, opscheck refuses to start (exit 64) rather than passing a check it cannot evaluate.
walBacklogMonitoring.rollbackRequirement: Rollback is not complete until the backlog is verified drained — readyCount back to 0 and archived_count advancing between two readings.

archivePushCoupling.behaviour: archive-push pushes to ALL configured repos and throws if ANY repo errored, by design, so PostgreSQL does not recycle the segment.
archivePushCoupling.consequence: Adding repo2 puts WAL archive availability behind repo2's availability. An unreachable repo2 suspends archiving to repo1 as well.
archivePushCoupling.noOptOut: There is no per-repo 'best effort' setting in 2.50.
archivePushCoupling.unchangedByThisDecision: This coupling is created by configuring repo2 at all, not by which topology is chosen. It is identical under A, B and C, and it is what the WAL backlog monitoring exists to detect.

explicitNonClaims: Does not close R-030, R-030-DB or R-030-FILES.
Does not authorize runbook §16.5, §22, or any production configuration change.
Is not production verification. Every result is OBSERVED_LOCAL_ONLY on a pinned local build; production's filesystem, WAL rate, network and load are not reproduced.
Does not procure, provision, or select a vendor.
Does not upgrade production pgBackRest, and does not recommend doing so before R-030-DB.
Does not prove failure-domain independence. A container on the same docker network is no model of an independent Türkiye host.
Does not establish Türkiye residency for anything. A hostname is not residency evidence and neither is a bucket name.
Does not measure production RPO or RTO.
remainingExternalBlockers: Türkiye residency evidence E1-E5 not obtained, E5 (backup/snapshot region) most often skipped
hosting DPA scoped to KVKK Art. 6 special-category health data not executed
subprocessor register §1 second hosting entry and §6 correction not made — required BEFORE any byte leaves production
no repo2-sourced restore drill has ever run
